xenophon.s: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier, historian and philosopher of the late fifth and fourth centuries BCE, a pupil of Socrates. He served with the Greek mercenaries hired by Cyrus the Younger in 401 BCE and led their retreat after Cyrus's death.

xerxes-i.s: Xerxes I was king of the Achaemenid Empire from 486 to 465 BCE, the son and successor of Darius I. He led the great invasion of Greece in 480 BCE, which won at Thermopylae and sacked Athens but was defeated at Salamis and, in 479 BCE, at Plataea.

xianbei.s: The Xianbei were a nomadic people of the eastern Eurasian steppe, in present-day Mongolia and Manchuria. After the decline of the Xiongnu, they became the dominant power on the northern steppe in the second century CE.

xiang-army.s: The Xiang Army was a regional military force raised in Hunan province by the scholar-official Zeng Guofan to fight the Taiping Rebellion. Its success, together with Li Hongzhang's Huai Army, was crucial in suppressing the Taiping.

xiang-jun.s: The xiang jun was the professional standing army of the Song Dynasty. The Song Dynasty profile notes that it was very large, with estimates of over one million men under arms at its peak.

xiang-yu.s: Xiang Yu was a Chinese military leader who led the rebellion against the Qin dynasty and became the dominant warlord after its fall. He then fought Liu Bang for control of China in the Chu–Han contention.

xiangyang.s: Xiangyang is a city on the Han River in central China, which with its twin city Fancheng formed the gateway to the Yangtze valley. The Mongol siege of Xiangyang from 1267 to 1273 was the pivotal confrontation in the conquest of the Southern Song.

xing-ware.s: Xing ware is a type of white porcelain produced at kilns in northern China under the Tang Dynasty. Its fine white body made it one of the earliest high-quality porcelains.

xinhai-revolution.s: The Xinhai Revolution was the revolution of 1911 that overthrew the Qing Empire and ended imperial rule in China. It was triggered by a military mutiny at Wuchang and spread rapidly as provinces declared independence.

xinjiang.s: Xinjiang is a large region in north-western China, including the Tarim Basin and Dzungaria, historically home to oasis cities on the Silk Road. Its eastern parts formed part of the domains of the Chagatai Empire and its successors.

xiongnu-civil-war.s: The Xiongnu civil war was a succession conflict among rival claimants to the position of chanyu that split the Xiongnu Empire around 57 BCE. The confederation divided between factions led by Huhanye, who submitted to the Han Dynasty, and his brother Zhizhi, who moved westward.

xiongnu-empire.s: The Xiongnu Empire was a confederation of nomadic peoples that dominated the eastern Eurasian steppe from the late third century BCE to the first century CE. Under the chanyu Modu it united the steppe tribes and became a formidable rival of the Han Dynasty, extracting tribute…

xoconusco.s: Xoconusco, or Soconusco, is a region on the Pacific coast of southern Mexico, in modern Chiapas, renowned for its cacao. The Aztec Empire profile records that the ruler Ahuitzotl extended the empire south to Xoconusco and into what is now Guatemala.

xuanwu-gate-incident.s: The Xuanwu Gate Incident was a palace coup in 626 CE in which Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers, the crown prince Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, at the Xuanwu Gate of the Tang palace in Chang'an. His father, Emperor Gaozu, soon abdicated in his favour.

xwastak.s: Xwastak was the land tax of the Sasanian Empire. The Sasanian Empire profile explains that the fiscal system rested on this tax, assessed on agricultural production.
